pre-fix-yarn.meaning: "November 22 through December 20, 2024" preserves the original year rather than correcting it; all office, price, tag and eligibility details survive.
pre-fix-yarn.sense: "first dibs" correctly expresses priority; "skinny little trees" conveys small diameter.
pre-fix-yarn.authenticity: "Give us a ring" and "find a feed" are natural Australian expressions.
pre-fix-yarn.register: "cos it matters", "does the bush a good turn" and "find a feed" make the body noticeably broader than the requested light level 2.
pre-fix-yarn.tone: "Have a good read of the overview" maintains the practical advisory purpose.
pre-fix-yarn.flow: "That depends on the weather and the supply" reads as a clear spoken explanation.
pre-fix-yarn.variety: "Chrissy" recurs throughout almost every tree reference, making the diminutive conspicuous.
pre-fix-yarn.essence: "One tag covers a tree up to 5 inches" retains the administrative detail and forest-health explanation that distinguish the notice.

current.meaning: "November 13, 2025" and "November 22 through December 20, 2024" preserve both dates, and all fees and tag thresholds remain.
current.sense: "Get in touch with us" preserves the unrestricted contact instruction, and "first priority" conveys the allocation rule.
current.authenticity: "Have a look here" and "does the forest some good too" sound natural and unforced.
current.register: "Chrissy tree permit" provides a light touch, with modest spoken recasting in "Give the overview and need-to-know information a careful read before you buy."
current.tone: "you’ll need another tag" keeps the instruction clear and suitably serious.
current.flow: "Buying through recreation.gov adds a $2.50 service fee" is concise and easily read aloud.
current.variety: "Have a look", "Get in touch" and "for instance" vary the transitions without repeated slang.
current.essence: "Local forest health experts pick out areas" retains the distinctive explanatory ending and practical notice structure.

dinkum-3.meaning: "Year 4 kids" recasts a US fourth-grade eligibility category as an Australian school-year label, while dates, fees and dimensions otherwise remain.
dinkum-3.sense: "first dibs" correctly expresses priority and "patches of feed" reasonably conveys forage.
dinkum-3.authenticity: "have a proper read" and "does the bush a good turn" are credible local speech.
dinkum-3.register: "just pop in", "heads up" and "skinny little trees" give the whole notice a broader voice than level 2 asks for.
dinkum-3.tone: "Make sure you have a proper read" preserves the practical advisory force.
dinkum-3.flow: "Buy one online through recreation.gov and there's an extra $2.50 service fee on top." is smooth explanatory speech.
dinkum-3.variety: "Chrissie" repeats in most references to the trees and permits, drawing attention to itself.
dinkum-3.essence: "Anything taller than 10 feet and/or wider than 5 inches needs an extra tag" retains the unusually specific permit mechanics and the forest-benefit ending.

pre-fix-yarn.quote: Cutting a Chrissy tree does the bush a good turn, too.
pre-fix-yarn.original: Cutting a Christmas tree also improves forest health.
pre-fix-yarn.why: Representative of a broadly colloquial body beyond the light level-2 request.
Chrissy is repeated at nearly every opportunity instead of varied naturally.

dinkum-3.why: Eligibility belongs to a US programme; replacing the school-system category with Year 4 can mislead a reader applying an Australian label.

dinkum-3.quote: And cutting a Chrissie tree does the bush a good turn, too.
dinkum-3.original: Cutting a Christmas tree also improves forest health.
dinkum-3.why: The broad conversational recasting across the body exceeds the requested light level 2.
The diminutive recurs conspicuously throughout the notice.

summaries.pre-fix-yarn: Complete and natural, but broader and more repetitive than a light treatment.
summaries.current: Faithful, clear notice with the right light Australian weight.
summaries.dinkum-3: Readable and complete in most respects, but too broad for level 2 and with a less exact eligibility label.
